The slow pacing of the campaign is completely gone and it's unfathomable that GGG can't create their new and improved game without just importing all of POE1's mechanics. Why take the time to make an entirely new game when it does not add anything new?

The game is going through a huge identity crisis right now. They want to slow down the gameplay, which is fair — I don't mind that. The problem is that many of the currently implemented systems don't fit well into that vision yet. Proper crafting doesn't exist, and combined with the very low loot drop rates, playing self-found mode feels like a slog and just isn't enjoyable. However, the visuals and audio are the best of any ARPG out there.

Path of Exile 2 is shit in its current state (Version 0.3).

This game is full of of decisions that can screw you over - sometimes instantly, sometimes hours later. The game also doesn't give you enough resources to recover from those decisions. At this point you either remake your character or follow (hopefully the right) guide, which kills all freedom for experimentation.

I’ve never written a Steam review before, because no other game has pissed me off this much. This should tell you how frustrated I am. Save yourself the pain and wait until the devs hopefully wake up from their fever dream of designing everything around infinite-resource late game players and finally decide to fix their game by giving new players the basic luxury of making early mistakes without ruining their entire progression.

This game has crazy potential, but it needs a massive overhaul before it is worth anyone's time.

The game looks and sounds great, with engaging and deep gameplay that offers plenty of build diversity. The endgame, although I haven’t fully experienced it, is rich with content, and considering it’s still in early access, that’s a great sign. Animations feel smooth and polished. Occasional lag spikes occur here and there, but they don’t significantly impact the overall experience. To me, boss fights are the best part of this game, period. Killing them brings a level of satisfaction I’ve never experienced in any other ARPG in a long time. Microtransactions are fair and reasonably priced, without feeling predatory like in *laugh* Diablo 4.

This is a Diablo-like game 
- Sold as a Path of Exile succesor
- Get loot as you massacre horde of enemies.

Pretending to be a Souls-like game 
- Highlight one-on-one encounters with bosses
- Dodge / Shield mechanics
- Balance resources mid combat
- Loss progress on death.

Where everything feels more like a gatcha game 
- Random maps
- Random game mechanics
- Random loot
- Random crafting
- Random targeting system
- Random accuracy
- Almost random armor (some white monster hit you and do nothing, just for the next hit one-shot you)

Path of Exile 2: Now Featuring the Revolutionary Concept of Negative Progression! 🎉

(TL,DR: Come for the loot. Stay for the emotional damage.)

Started off fun. Had a blast leveling, exploring builds, and dreaming of the possibilities. Then I hit the endgame... and that's when the real fun began — if your idea of fun is watching hours of effort vanish into the void.

Endgame isn't hard. It's punishing. You don’t get challenged — you get slapped around, lose your maps, waste your resources, and then get to do it all over again… slower. It’s less about mastering mechanics and more about mastering your ability to tolerate setbacks that feel designed just to waste your time.

Build diversity? Oh sure, there are "options" — as long as you enjoy dealing zero damage or getting one-shot for daring to try something creative. Stray from the meta, and the game gently (read: violently) reminds you that you’ve made a terrible mistake.

There’s a beautiful game buried under all this. But unless you enjoy losing progress, resources, and your will to live — maybe wait until they stop confusing "challenging" with "utterly demoralizing."

Season 1 was pretty fun but honestly after all this time and the direction the game is going I cannot find ONE reason that somebody would want to move from POE1 to POE2.

The game promised a more nuanced and tactical combat and in a few months the design team got completely bullied into making the game mechanics like POE1, except that you die faster, the game is much less balanced and Melee is an absolute dumpster fire (not that it was good in POE1 but at least that's a complete game, this one isn't).

If you don't like ARPG I don't recommend the game, if you like POE1 I also don't recommend switching until, if ever, a clearer design direction is realized by the new team, otherwise this is just a less optimized and balanced POE1.

And for god's sake increase the goddamn drop rates, having a crafting system and putting it behind hundred of hours of farming has been getting on my nerves, as a non-unemployed person.
